title: 4 Korean words for when you're ANGRY 😤 …just not in front of your boss #learnkorean
caption:
Bad day? Here's how Koreans say it:

짜증 나 (jja-jeung na) = So annoying!
열받아 (yeol-ba-da) = I'm boiling! (literally "I'm getting heated")
어이없어 (eo-i-eop-sseo) = Unbelievable… I'm speechless.
억울해 (eo-gul-hae) = That's so unfair! (when you get blamed for something you didn't do)

All four are casual. Use them with friends. In front of elders or your boss, smile, say 네, 사장님~ (ne, sa-jang-nim = Yes, boss~) and keep it in your head 😅

pinnedComment: Which one do you need most? 짜증 나 · 열받아 · 어이없어 · 억울해 👇
alt: A needle-felted comedy about one bad day, with an anger gauge on the left. A coral felt mascot misses the bus and gets splashed with muddy water: 짜증 나! (jja-jeung na) = So annoying! Someone takes the last kimbap and it turns into a whistling kettle on a stove: 열받아! (yeol-ba-da) = I am boiling! The friend who owes it money shows off new shoes and its soul floats out on a park bench: 어이없어… (eo-i-eop-sseo) = Unbelievable… A cat knocks a cup off the cafe counter and the mascot gets blamed, crying: 억울해! (eo-gul-hae) = That is so unfair! With the gauge full, the boss walks over and the mascot smiles: 네, 사장님~ (ne, sa-jang-nim) = Yes, boss~ while a volcano erupts above its head with 억울해!! inside. Closing line: With elders and bosses, keep it in your head! The cat pushes another cup off the counter.
